## CAP-12 Attachments

Attachments carry large binary data outside the document. Create one, store its token in
a field **declared `ATTACHMENT`**, then fetch it on any peer that has the token. The block
is generated from a test that CI runs (local create → insert → select → fetch):

<!-- snippet: rust-attachments -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-snippets.py from code CI runs. Edit the marked source, not this block. -->
```rust
use dittolive_ditto::store::attachment::DittoAttachmentFetchEvent;

async fn attach_and_fetch(store: &Store, bytes: &[u8]) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let metadata = HashMap::from([("name".to_string(), "photo.jpg".to_string())]);
    let attachment = store.new_attachment_from_bytes(bytes, metadata).await?;
    // The field must be declared ATTACHMENT, with the COLLECTION keyword.
    store
        .execute((
            "INSERT INTO COLLECTION photos (image ATTACHMENT) DOCUMENTS (:doc)",
            json!({ "doc": { "_id": "p1", "image": attachment } }),
        ))
        .await?;

    let result = store
        .execute("SELECT * FROM COLLECTION photos (image ATTACHMENT) WHERE _id = 'p1'")
        .await?;
    let item = result
        .get_item(0)
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("p1 missing"))?;
    let value = item.value();
    let token = value
        .get("image")
        .and_then(|image| image.as_object())
        .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("no attachment token"))?;

    let (tx, rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
    let tx = std::sync::Mutex::new(Some(tx));
    let _fetcher = store.fetch_attachment(token, move |event| match event {
        DittoAttachmentFetchEvent::Progress {
            downloaded_bytes,
            total_bytes,
        } => {
            println!("{downloaded_bytes}/{total_bytes} bytes");
        }
        DittoAttachmentFetchEvent::Completed { attachment } => {
            if let Some(tx) = tx.lock().ok().and_then(|mut slot| slot.take()) {
                let _ = tx.send(attachment.path());
            }
        }
        DittoAttachmentFetchEvent::Deleted => println!("attachment deleted"),
    })?;
    let path = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), rx).await??;
    println!("attachment file: {}", path.display());
    Ok(())
}
```
<!-- /snippet -->

```text
Store::new_attachment(&self, path: &impl AsRef<Path>, metadata: HashMap<String, String>) -> Result<DittoAttachment>   (async)
Store::new_attachment_from_bytes(&self, bytes: &impl AsRef<[u8]>, metadata: HashMap<String, String>) -> Result<DittoAttachment>   (async)
Store::fetch_attachment(&self, token: impl DittoAttachmentTokenLike,
                        on_event: impl Fn(DittoAttachmentFetchEvent) + Send + Sync + 'static) -> Result<DittoAttachmentFetcher>
```

## Rules

- **Declare the field:** `INSERT INTO COLLECTION photos (image ATTACHMENT) DOCUMENTS …`
  and the same `COLLECTION photos (image ATTACHMENT)` on `SELECT`/`UPDATE`. Without
  `COLLECTION` the statement fails `DqlQueryCompilation`. Without the declaration nothing
  fails: the token is stored as an ordinary map (executed), which the documentation says
  is not an attachment reference.
- **The token** is `item.value().get("image")?.as_object()`, a
  `&BTreeMap<CborValue, CborValue>`; `fetch_attachment` also accepts a
  `DittoAttachmentToken`. `DittoAttachment` implements `Serialize`, so it goes straight
  into query arguments.
- **Metadata** is `HashMap<String, String>` only.
- **Events** (`DittoAttachmentFetchEvent`): `Progress { downloaded_bytes, total_bytes }`,
  `Completed { attachment }`, `Deleted`. The callback runs on a Ditto thread and is `Fn`,
  so a one-shot sender needs a `Mutex<Option<_>>` as above. Completion of a local
  attachment is immediate; from a peer it waits for sync.
- **The fetcher keeps running when dropped**; call `fetcher.cancel()` to stop it. It
  unregisters itself on `Completed` or `Deleted`. `store.attachment_fetchers()` lists the
  active ones.
- `attachment.path()` is a file inside Ditto's persistence directory: read or copy it,
  never modify or delete it. It panics if the `Ditto` has been dropped.
- `new_attachment` copies the file synchronously inside its first poll; for large files
  run it in `spawn_blocking` ([tokio.md](tokio.md#heavy-queries-off-the-async-workers)).
  A non-UTF-8 path panics.
- Size limits, garbage collection and sync behaviour:
  <https://docs.ditto.live/sdk/latest/crud/working-with-attachments>.
